references.text: Micah describes a similar curse where the people will press olives but not anoint themselves with oil, as a judgment from God over disobedience.
Amos mentions the destruction of olive trees as part of God's judgment on Israel, parallel to the threat that the olive trees will lose their fruit.
Joel describes the destruction of olive trees and the loss of oil as part of a national catastrophe, similar to the curse in Deuteronomy.
God's promise of blessing over the land includes olive trees, which stands in contrast to the curse where the olive trees lose their fruit.
